status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Ethiopian translation text for 3 John (1 chapter, 14 verses) is content-identical to the KJV rendering already indexed for this book — same four named figures (the elder, Gaius, Diotrephes, Demetrius), same single collective group (brethren/strangers), same closing greetings, no additional or missing verses, no deuterocanonical variance (unlike this Ethiopian Bible's own Ezra/1-Esdras divergence elsewhere). Adapted the already-validated KJV structure (4 person-type manager tiers, no law tiers, one submanager) rather than inventing a new shape, per the task's own guidance for shared-canon books that turn out identical. IDs suffixed "_ethiopian" and tier names re-verified word-for-word against this translation's own extracted text before reuse. Naming-collision flags carried over and re-confirmed against this text: this Gaius is not identified with the Gaius of Corinth (Romans 16:23/1 Corinthians 1:14), Macedonia (Acts 19:29), or Derbe (Acts 20:4); this Demetrius is not identified with the silversmith of Acts 19:24-41; "the elder" is only ever self-designated that way in the text (matching 2 John 1:1) — traditional identification with John the Apostle/Evangelist is tradition, not textual fact, and is not asserted here. No genealogy (parents/spouses/children) or ageEvents are stated anywhere in this short personal letter for any figure — all such fields are empty/null. The one collective figure, "the brethren and strangers" Gaius supported (3 John 1:5-8), is kept as a single loyalty-boost submanager under Gaius rather than invented as individuals, since the text never differentiates them, matching this book's already-validated KJV structure.

characters.name: The Elder

verses.note: The elder writes to the wellbeloved Gaius, whom he loves in the truth.
Has no greater joy than to hear his children walk in truth.
Wrote to the church, but Diotrephes refuses to receive him and speaks maliciously against him.
Has many things to write but prefers to speak face to face rather than with ink and pen.

funFacts: Self-designated only as "the elder" in this letter, the same title used in 2 John 1:1 — traditional identification with John the Apostle/Evangelist is not asserted as textual fact here.

characters.name: Gaius

verses.note: The wellbeloved recipient of the letter; the elder wishes he may prosper and be in health.
Brethren testified of the truth in him, that he walks in the truth.
Faithfully supports the brethren and strangers, sending them forward on their journey in a godly manner, taking nothing of the Gentiles.

funFacts: Not identified with the Gaius of Corinth (Romans 16:23/1 Corinthians 1:14), Macedonia (Acts 19:29), or Derbe (Acts 20:4) — naming collision flagged, not merged.

verses.note: Brethren and strangers whom Gaius supported on their journey; they bore witness of his charity before the church and went forth for the Name's sake, taking nothing of the Gentiles.
Loves to have the preeminence among the church and refuses to receive the elder.
Prates against the elder with malicious words, refuses to receive the brethren, forbids others who would, and casts them out of the church.

characters.name: Demetrius

verses.note: Has good report of all men and of the truth itself; the elder and others bear record that it is true.

funFacts: Not identified with the silversmith Demetrius of Acts 19:24-41 — naming collision flagged, not merged.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk or deliberately-unresolved references, kept out of the character list above.

friends_greeting.note: "Our friends salute thee. Greet the friends by name" — unnamed collective well-wishers on both ends of the correspondence, not individually identified.

spiritual_children.note: "My children" — the elder's spiritual converts/disciples in general, not named individuals; no biological family is mentioned for the elder anywhere in this letter.

the_church.note: "The church" the elder wrote to, and from which Diotrephes casts out willing brethren — the congregation itself, not a person, kept out of the character list.
